findings.description: verify() rehashes and re-extracts each clean package proof's retainedArchive (178-190) but never reads registry['retainedArchive'] (.local/artifacts/scm-sdk-0.2.2-registry-c908cad8b27863d0.crate). limitations: Read-only review: I could not execute commands, so recorded exit codes, digests and receipts were inspected rather than recomputed. I verified internal consistency (registry archiveSha256 equals both clean proofs' archive_sha256; the CI context list equals the workflow matrix I read; the projections.json row count equals the test's hard assertion) but could not rerun the 59-command gate or the clean archive builds.

I could not recompute SHA-256 digests with the available tools, so producerSha256, verifierSha256, guardSha256, checks_sha256 and the prompt/CLI digests are accepted as recorded. A mismatch between a recorded digest and current file bytes would not have been detected here; the gate tooling does enforce several of these at --advance time.

No network access, so the crates.io publication, the Forgejo run status and the SSH ls-remote tag observation are accepted from retained receipts under the repository-writer trust boundary documented in docs/PHASES.md and restated in the receipts' own limitations.

The archives (.local/artifacts/*.crate) and the .local producer scripts are outside the git tree and were not opened; their content is assessed only through the producer source and digests embedded in the receipts, which is exactly the supportability gap recorded in finding 2.
I did not read any credential, token or tenant-registration file, so the claim that no secrets are present rests on the recorded private-material scans rather than my own inspection.

The bound 59-command snapshot (09:02) predates publication (09:12), tag and CI (09:18-09:45). I treated this as adequately mitigated because the full 34-test test_ci.py suite was rerun post-publication at 09:13, the activated guard branch was traced at 09:55, and release_delivery.verify() re-binds the published and CI commits to the same reviewed fingerprint; but no complete 59-command rerun exists against the final bookkeeping state, and the maintainer has deliberately frozen that snapshot because the candidate checker binds git HEAD.

Because the reviewed source fingerprint is unchanged from attempt 4 and is cryptographically bound into the registry readiness and CI receipts, the four unresolved attempt-4 findings cannot be fixed inside phase 20 without invalidating the delivery evidence. I scored them as remaining deficiencies rather than as correctable defects, and I did not treat the deferral itself as dishonest.

I reviewed phase 20's acceptance criteria and the cumulative G25 change it qualifies; I did not re-audit phases 1-17 historical infrastructure, and items explicitly recorded as future work (generated projection-field rustdoc, broad unpaired-root pairing diagnostics) were treated as out of this patch's scope rather than as missing deliverables.
